input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Section 4(c) is the only licence to us, and it runs to "Company" alone — a term defined in the preamble as Clear Capital, with no affiliate coverage anywhere in the Agreement. Nothing makes the licence transferable to a successor either; Section 10 instead bars either party from assigning or transferring the Agreement or its obligations without the other's prior written consent, so an M&A successor cannot rely on the grant. The licence is helpfully perpetual, royalty-free and sublicensable, but it fails both fallback elements (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor) on material terms. We therefore target the fallback and add only those two features to the existing grant, leaving the rest of Section 4(c) and Section 10 untouched.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 4(c) licence to Company's affiliates on written notice and make it transferable to an M&A successor without Contractor's approval.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our fallback licence position requires affiliate coverage on written notice and transferability to a successor in a merger or acquisition, so we have added both to the Section 4(c) grant and confirmed the successor transfer needs no Contractor approval given the consent requirement in Section 10.

ops.newText: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company and its affiliates (on written notice to Contractor) a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense), transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition without Contractor's approval, to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
